question: What is the radius of the striking or shooting circle in hockey?.
solution:
The correct answer is __**14.63 meters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The radius of the striking or shooting circle in hockey is **14.63 meters**, as per the official rules of the International Hockey Federation (FIH).
 
• This circle is often referred to as the "D" or the "shooting circle" due to its semicircular shape.
 
• The striking circle is the area from where players can legally score a goal if the ball is hit within its boundary.
 
• The measurement is taken from the center of the goal line to the outer edge of the circle.
 
• This dimension is standardized for all international hockey games to maintain uniformity in play.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shooting Circle:** The area where players can shoot the ball to score a goal, provided the ball is touched by an attacker inside this zone.
 
• **Penalty Corner:** Awarded to the attacking team for a foul committed by the defending team inside the shooting circle.
 
• **Goal Dimensions:** The width of the goal in field hockey is 3.66 meters, and its height is 2.14 meters.
 
• **Field Dimensions:** A standard field hockey pitch measures 91.4 meters in length and 55 meters in width.
 
• **Field Markings:** In addition to the striking circle, the pitch includes 23-meter lines, a centerline, and sidelines for game organization and rule enforcement.
